days.title: Guwahati to Shillong — the temple, the lake, the hill town

stops.title: Kamakhya Temple
stops.notes: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas, on Nilachal hill above the Brahmaputra. No entry fee; phones stay outside, and the climb back up is steep in the rain

stops.title: Highway lunch at Umiam
stops.notes: Jadoh and doh-nei-iong, the Khasi pork-and-rice dish — the lakeside shacks do it better than the town restaurants

stops.title: Umiam Lake viewpoint
stops.notes: A reservoir ringed by pine on the Shillong road — the viewpoint is free, the boats and water sports are not

stops.title: Police Bazaar, Shillong
stops.notes: The town's walking heart — the evening is a slow circuit of the square, the cafes and the music shops

stops.title: First night in Shillong
stops.notes: Guesthouses around Laitumkhrah are quieter and cheaper than the Police Bazaar hotels

days.title: Shillong to Cherrapunji — the wettest place on earth

stops.title: Elephant Falls
stops.notes: Three tiers of falls ten minutes out of town, with steps down to the pool. A small state entry is collected at the gate (see the ticket allowance)

stops.title: Nohkalikai Falls
stops.notes: India's tallest plunge waterfall, off a cliff-edge viewpoint — the green pool at the bottom is the photograph. The Khasi legend behind the name is worth asking a local guide about

stops.title: Mawsmai Caves
stops.notes: A lit limestone cave you walk right through, about 150 m of it — the one Sohra stop that rain cannot cancel. Small entry fee at the gate (allowance)

stops.title: Night in Sohra
stops.notes: Stay on the Sohra side of the plateau, not back in Shillong — tomorrow's road east starts here

days.title: East to Mawlynnong, Asia's cleanest village — and a living root bridge

stops.title: Seven Sisters Falls (Nohsngithiang)
stops.notes: Seven separate falls on the same cliff line — five minutes from Mawsmai, so pair them. Best in the post-monsoon months when there is water

stops.title: Riwai living root bridge
stops.notes: A footbridge grown — not built — from the aerial roots of a rubber fig, and still alive. This one is a short walk from the road, unlike the famous double-decker at Nongriat, which is 3,000 steps down

stops.title: Mawlynnong village and the sky walk
stops.notes: Widely called Asia's cleanest village, run as a cooperative — bamboo dustbins on every lane, a bamboo sky walk above the treetops, and a village entry fee at the gate (allowance)

stops.title: Night at the river, Dawki
stops.notes: Sleeping at Shnongpdeng or Dawki puts you on the Umngot at sunrise — the only hour the river is mirror-flat and empty

days.title: The Umngot river, then back up to Shillong

stops.title: Umngot river boat at Dawki
stops.notes: The clearest river in India — you see the riverbed metres down, and a boat can look like it is floating on glass. Boats are chartered, not ticketed: ₹300–1,200 depending on length and season (see the expense line). Go before 10 AM

stops.title: Laitlum Canyons
stops.notes: A canyon rim with no railings, no ticket counter and no crowd on a weekday — the road up is steep and the pay-off is the whole Khasi hill range

stops.title: Second night in Shillong
stops.notes: Back in the same town on purpose — the drive north tomorrow starts three hours from the airport

days.title: Shillong Peak, then the road down to Guwahati

stops.title: Shillong Peak
stops.notes: The state's highest motorable point above the town — clear mornings open up the Bangladesh plains. Go early before the cloud sits in

stops.title: Lunch on arrival in Guwahati
stops.notes: The highway drops you into the city in about three hours; eat here rather than detouring — the airport road runs through the other side of town

stops.title: Down NH6 to Guwahati
stops.notes: About three hours from Shillong when the highway behaves; leave by early afternoon for an evening flight out

expenses.label: Umngot river boat at Dawki (chartered per boat, ₹300–₹1,200 depending on length and season)
Meghalaya state tickets and village entries not itemised (Mawsmai, Nohkalikai, Seven Sisters, Elephant Falls, Riwai root bridge, Mawlynnong gate)

publication.title: Meghalaya — Rain, Caves & Living Root Bridges
publication.tagline: Cherrapunji's cliff-edge falls, a footbridge grown from tree roots and a night beside India's clearest river — the Northeast's best five days, and its cheapest.
publication.bestSeason: Sep–Nov and Mar–Apr — post-monsoon falls run full with passable roads. Jun–Aug is the 10,000 mm season: spectacular, and often literally washed out
travelTips: Base the middle two nights at Sohra and Dawki rather than commuting from Shillong — the plateau roads are slow and you want the early hours.
Visit Riwai's root bridge, not Nongriat's. Riwai is a short walk from the road; the famous double-decker is 3,000 steps down and 3,000 back up.
Book the Umngot boat for first light. The river is glass before 10 AM and brown after rain.
Carry cash for every gate: the caves, the falls viewpoints, the root bridge and the Mawlynnong entry all collect locally.
Hire a local driver who knows the Sohra–Mawlynnong road. It is not a highway, and the fog is real.
warningsAndAssumptions: Meghalaya's state-run caves, waterfalls and village viewpoints charge small per-person tickets (typically ₹10–₹100) that are collected in cash at each gate and revised locally. They are deliberately NOT itemised as stop fees here — a ₹250/person ticket allowance covers all of them.

Umngot river boats are chartered per boat, not ticketed per person: 2026 sources range from ₹300–₹500 for 20–30 minutes to ₹1,000–₹1,200 for a longer ride. ₹400/person is budgeted for a shared 45-minute ride.
Kamakhya Temple has no entry fee; photography inside is prohibited and phones are not allowed past the outer gate.
Nohkalikai and the Seven Sisters falls are seasonal — in the dry winter months they reduce to a trickle, and this trip is planned for the post-monsoon window when they run full.
Mawlynnong's entry, and the Riwai root bridge, are managed by village committees; the fees support the community and are collected by hand.
The Guwahati–Shillong road (NH6) is winding and takes about three hours; road-widening work and monsoon landslides can add an hour.
All costs are engine estimates over real coordinates and cited fees, not quotes. Treat ±15% as the honest band.
